title: Russia plague scare
ticker: BREAKING: Plague lab worker's death in Siberia sparks fears in Russia
About 200 contacts placed under medical observation in Irkutsk
Russia tells WHO: "no plague case", no pathogens detected
U.S. formally requests information from Russia
WHO asks Moscow about reports of a second suspicious pneumonia death

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Good evening, and welcome to KOWEN News.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: In Siberia, a young woman who worked at a *plague research laboratory* has died.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Around *two hundred people* have been placed under medical observation, and hospitals have been put under quarantine.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Russia insists it was *not plague*. But experts say the official story doesn't add up.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: And with the world still remembering *COVID*, every unanswered question matters.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Tonight: what we know, what we don't, and why the world is *worried*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The woman was a lab technician at the *Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute*, in southeastern Siberia.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Independent outlets identified her as a twenty eight year old employee named *Darya*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: According to Russian media reports, she told medical staff she had *accidentally broken a test tube* containing live bacteria while collecting samples.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: She was hospitalised on September twenty ninth with symptoms of *severe pneumonia*, in the town of Shelekhov near Irkutsk.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: She was placed on a ventilator, and *died* on October second.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: What killed her is still unclear, and officials have *contradicted each other*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Irkutsk's governor first spoke only of a suspected *particularly dangerous infection*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The head of neighbouring Buryatia said she had *died of plague*. His statement was later edited to say she had *possibly* died from plague.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Russia's health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, says she died of pneumonia of *unknown origin*, and that her illness was not linked to her work.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Yet the response on the ground has been *dramatic*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: At least *one hundred ninety seven* people who may have had contact with her were placed under medical observation, more than a hundred of them in hospital wards.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The hospital in Shelekhov was put under *quarantine*. Public events in Irkutsk were cancelled.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Police reportedly opened a *criminal investigation* into possible health safety violations resulting in death.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Local media reported that *sixty workers* at the anti-plague institute were also in quarantine.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: She was forty weeks pregnant, and had to *change hospitals* after new quarantine rules meant her husband could no longer be with her during labor.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: One pregnant woman told CNN that at her maternity hospital, she was given a questionnaire titled *checklist for suspected highly dangerous infectious disease plague*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Some neighbouring regions introduced *quarantine controls* at their borders.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Residents are divided. One said ambulance doctors are driving around in *full Covid protective suits*. Another said everything is as usual, no visible changes.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Neighbouring countries are not taking chances.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan have introduced *quarantine controls* at border crossings.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: China, however, does not appear to have added border measures, and flights from Irkutsk to China have *not been cancelled*, according to CNN.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Moscow, however, says there is *nothing to fear*.

scenes.name: Rospotrebnadzor
scenes.quote: No epidemic risk. Over 90% of contacts checked. No dangerous pathogens found.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Russia's health watchdog says there is *no epidemic risk*, and that it is winding down its response.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It says medical checks have been completed for *over ninety percent* of her contacts, and no dangerous pathogens have been found.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The Kremlin says it informed the *World Health Organization* in accordance with established practice.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The Kremlin has urged people to rely on the watchdog's updates, rather than *rumors and speculation*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Irkutsk's governor says all known contacts are under observation, show *no signs of illness*, and have tested negative.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The WHO says Russian regulators told it there is *no plague case*, and no evidence pneumonic plague played a part in her death.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Based on unofficial information, the WHO says the public health risk to the general population appears to be *low*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: But the agency has asked Moscow for *lab results*, tests and further analysis.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It has also asked about media reports of *a second* suspicious pneumonia death in the region.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: CNN says it is not aware of any such second case, and *no local media or officials* have confirmed one.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: We want to put out fair, factual information, said the WHO's Maria Van Kerkhove, *and when we don't have an answer, we say so*.

scenes.name: Jennifer Nuzzo
scenes.quote: If it's plague, breathe a sigh of relief, because we know what to do about plague.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Experts say the pieces *don't fit*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: If a lab worker is exposed to plague, they take antibiotics. *You'd be fine*, said Jennifer Nuzzo of Brown University's Pandemic Center. You don't die, typically.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Quarantining two hundred people for a single case of pneumonia would be *unusual*, she said.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: If it's plague, breathe a sigh of relief, because we know what to do about plague. *The worry is it's not that*.

scenes.name: Dr. Ashish Jha
scenes.role: Former White House COVID coordinator · TIME
scenes.quote: You can't help but worry that there is something more here than meets the eye.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Dr. Ashish Jha, who led the White House COVID response under President Biden, raised a darker possibility: *an accidental release from a deliberate program*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Russia has a long history of *bioengineering pathogens*. The Soviet programs were officially shut down, but the current situation is unclear.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: You can't help but worry, Jha told TIME, that there is *something more here than meets the eye*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Jha said friends in the Trump administration have been *very worried*, but are not getting much information or data.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The Irkutsk institute was founded in *1934* to fight plague, and employs around ninety five researchers. Plague still circulates naturally in wildlife across parts of *Siberia*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Plague is caused by the bacterium *Yersinia pestis*, usually carried by small mammals and their fleas.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The most dangerous form, *pneumonic plague*, infects the lungs and can spread from person to person through the air.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Untreated, it can kill within *a day*. But common antibiotics cure it if given early.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Plague is not gone from the world. The WHO counted nearly *four thousand cases* and four hundred twenty three deaths in ten countries between 2019 and 2025.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: The case has now reached the *White House*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The United States has made a *formal request* to Russia for information.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said it is incumbent upon Russia to *share more information* with the world. Maybe it's bigger than we thought, he said. We don't know.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: President Trump says he expects to speak with Vladimir Putin about the issue. The Kremlin says no call has been arranged, but *could be*, if requested.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: With independent media restricted in Russia, much of what is known comes from small regional outlets, *Telegram channels*, and leaks from medical staff.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: As one expert put it, infectious disease surveillance only works if countries report *early and honestly*. Reporting for KOWEN News.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: To recap tonight's top story.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: A lab worker at a Siberian *anti-plague institute* has died of severe pneumonia, and about two hundred contacts have been isolated.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Russia says it was *not plague*, and that there is no epidemic risk. There is no confirmed outbreak.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: But the WHO and the United States are still *demanding answers*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Four Central Asian neighbours have added *quarantine checks* at their borders.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Until Russia shares its lab results, the question remains: *what really killed her?*

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: We'll keep following this story. That's all for tonight. This has been KOWEN News. Thanks for watching, and good night.
